prioritized_defects.description: The stride-scheduling execution loop is not modeled as a proper repeating loop with a clear continue/back-edge and termination condition; the diagram presents the loop header as a terminal decision and does not clearly show repetition after advancing the pass value.
prioritized_defects.evidence: The requirements specify that execution runs as long as there are jobs in the queues (R92), selects the minimum-pass job, allots a quantum, advances pass by stride, uses FIFO on ties, and repeats until no jobs remain (R95-R99). The diagram labels N40 as 'LOOP while Jobs left in queues? is [no]' and places the body under it, but the shown structure does not clearly encode a back-edge from N44 to N40 or a condition-driven repetition until no jobs are left. This makes the required iterative scheduling semantics ambiguous/incomplete.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Model the execution as an explicit loop with a guard 'jobs remain in queues', body actions in sequence, and a clear back-edge from advancing pass to the loop test, ending only when no jobs remain.

prioritized_defects.description: The submit-job gate conflates multiple required checks into one decision, obscuring the required distinction between submission openness, user validity, and the later accept/reject scheduling decision.
prioritized_defects.evidence: The requirements state that the cluster first decides whether it is open for job submissions and whether the user is valid (R43, R44), and that this is different from the Accept/Reject Job feature which applies only when the cluster is open (R45, R46). The diagram uses a single decision N7 'Submission allowed and user valid?' before entering all later features, and then routes to submission processing at N23. This merges distinct checks and does not preserve the required separation between eligibility to submit and later job acceptance based on budget/deadline.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Separate the submission-open check and user-validity check from the Accept/Reject Job logic, and route only the submit-job feature through the initial gate while keeping the accept/reject decision inside the job-processing path.

prioritized_defects.description: Step 'update cluster status' is drawn 3 times (N20, N38, N39).
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Draw a step shared by several branches once, before the decision or after the branches rejoin.

prioritized_defects.description: The cluster status update behavior is drawn multiple times on the same execution path, causing the required single update behavior to be represented redundantly.
prioritized_defects.evidence: The requirements specify update cluster status as a single feature behavior: after delete/change job it updates cluster status (R61), and cluster status is updated when a job is scheduled and also when a job ends (R87, R88). In the diagram, N20 updates cluster status after delete/change, N38 updates cluster status after scheduling, and N39 updates cluster status again for job end, without a clear semantic separation or merged trigger model.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Model cluster-status update once per triggering event, or clearly separate the distinct triggers with appropriate control flow so the same semantic update is not duplicated on one path.

final_recommendation: Prioritize the two HIGH-severity control-flow defects first, then address the duplicated cluster-status granularity defects.
